212	## parsed.json
213	
214	One object keyed by the `.eml` filename stem. **Every email in the directory must appear.**
215	
216	```json
217	{
218	  "E003": {
219	    "classification": "rfq",
220	    "revises": null,
221	    "duplicate_of": null,
222	    "needs_review": false,
223	    "review_reason": null,
224	    "line_items": [
225	      {
226	        "raw": "2\" x 21' - 12 lengths",
227	        "description": "2\" pipe, SCH 40 A53B ERW, threaded & coupled, 21' lengths",
228	        "qty": 12,
229	        "uom": "EA",
230	        "source": "body"
231	      }
232	    ]
233	  }
234	}
235	```
236	
237	### classification — exactly one per email
238	
239	| value | the **current** message … | line_items |
240	|---|---|---|
241	| `rfq` | asks us to price or check availability of items | the items |
242	| `rfq_revision` | changes a request made earlier in the same thread (quantities, additions, removals) | the **complete** order as now intended; `revises` = the earlier email's id if it is in the inbox, else null |
243	| `purchase_order` | commits to buy — a PO, "please process", "go ahead with items 1–3" | the items ordered |
244	| `vendor_quote` | is a supplier quoting or answering **us** | `[]` |
245	| `status_inquiry` | asks about an existing quote or order (update? ETA? tracking?) | `[]` |
246	| `auto_reply` | is machine-generated: out-of-office, bounce, receipt | `[]` |
247	| `other` | anything else: marketing, invoices and remittances, job applications, internal chatter, "we went with someone else" | `[]` |
248	
249	Classify what the current message *does* — not the subject line, not the quoted history.
250	
251	### line_items — one per thing the customer is asking for
252	
253	- **What counts.** Items in the current message, its attachments and pasted pictures, and —
254	  when one of our own reps forwards a customer's email — in the forwarded content. Not items
255	  in quoted earlier messages (they were handled when they arrived), not headings, notes,
256	  totals, prices, signatures, crossed-out lines, or old revisions of a document.
257	- **`raw`** — the line's text as it appears where you found it (a table row's cells on one
258	  line; for a picture or scan, your reading of it). We pair your lines with ours on these
259	  tokens, so keep it close to the source.
260	- **`description`** — the item **self-contained**, as an ISR would type it into a quote
261	  without re-reading the email: the line's own words plus every heading, note, column
262	  header, sheet name, form field, subject line or earlier line that applies to it — and
263	  nothing that doesn't apply to it. Never invent a spec the email doesn't give.
264	- **`qty` / `uom`** — as the customer stated it, not converted. A number spelled out is a
265	  number; a vague amount ("a couple", "enough for the job") is `null`. A size, schedule,
266	  length, rating, part number or price is never a quantity. `uom` is one of `EA FT M IN BX
267	  PK PR DZ RL LB SET GAL BAG CS`, or `null` when no unit is stated (we read `null` as `EA`).
268	- **`source`** — `"body"`, or the filename of the attachment / pasted image the line came from.
269	
270	### Threads, duplicates, forwards
271	
272	- A reply that changes an earlier request → `rfq_revision` with the **complete** order as the
273	  customer now intends it; the earlier email keeps its own lines as they were on arrival.
274	- The same request sent twice → **the email with the later `Date:` is the duplicate**: same
275	  classification as the original, `duplicate_of` = the original's id, `line_items: []`.
276	- Anything **from** `@ridgeline-supply.example` is one of our own reps, usually forwarding a
277	  customer's email; classify it as the customer's email, and read the rep's own note too.
278	
279	### needs_review — "a human has to look at this before anyone quotes it"
280	
281	`true` when the email asks for something you cannot fully read or resolve: the attachment it
282	points at is missing or can't be opened, or the items themselves are only identified by
283	something that isn't in the email ("same as our last order, but double it"). Put the reason in `review_reason` (required when `true`) and still
284	return whatever lines you *could* read. Only for `rfq`, `rfq_revision` and `purchase_order`.
285	
286	## Optional: matching to the catalog
287	
288	If you build the optional matcher, add three fields to each line item:
289	
290	```json
291	{"raw": "...", "description": "...", "qty": 12, "uom": "EA", "source": "body",
292	 "sku": "RL-12345", "match": "matched", "match_reason": "2\" 150# RF weld neck A105: one part fits"}
293	```
294	
295	- `match` is one of `matched` (exactly one catalog part is what the customer asked for —
296	  `sku` is it), `not_in_catalog` (we don't stock it — `sku: null`), or `ambiguous` (more than
297	  one stocked part fits what the customer wrote and they'd have to choose — `sku: null`,
298	  optional `candidates: [skus]`).
299	- `match_reason` — one short line a rep can check.
300	- **Not in catalog is a decision, not a failure.** Ridgeline doesn't stock everything
301	  customers ask for, and the nearest catalog part is often one attribute away — right size and
302	  type, wrong schedule, rating or material. Quoting that part is a wrong quote.
303	- `catalog.csv` columns: `sku, description, category, product, size, spec` (schedule or
304	  pressure class)`, material, ends, extra, uom`. Descriptions are abbreviated the way an ERP
305	  prints them.
306	
307	## World facts
308	
309	- Ridgeline Industrial Supply sells pipe, fittings, flanges, valves, gaskets, bolting and
310	  related industrial supplies. The RFQ inbox is `rfq@ridgeline-supply.example`.
311	- Our quotes are numbered `Q-26-…`. Customers' RFQ and PO numbers are theirs.
312	- A supplier answering *our* request for pricing is a `vendor_quote`, however much it looks
313	  like a list of items.
314	
315	## What we grade
316	
317	Your `parse` command on the held-out inbox, against our key, **before we read anything you wrote**.
318	
319	**Headline numbers** — the expensive failures, in this order:
320	1. **Silent losses** — an email that needed someone to act (it has items, or needs review)
321	   came back with no lines and no review flag. That customer never hears back.
322	2. **Hallucinated lines** — lines that aren't requests: quoted history, headings, prices,
323	   signatures, crossed-out or superseded rows.
324	3. **Lost and phantom requests** — a request classified as something else (lost), or a
325	   vendor quote / bounce / newsletter classified as a request (phantom).
326	
327	Then: classification accuracy, line recall and precision, and on paired lines — `qty`,
328	`uom`, `source`, and **context carried** (does the `description` mention what the key's
329	`must_mention` lists, and none of its `must_not_mention`?). Plus `revises` / `duplicate_of`
330	links and `needs_review` precision/recall.
331	
332	**Optional matcher**, if present: confident wrong matches (you named a part; the answer was a
333	different part, *not in catalog*, or *ambiguous*), not-in-catalog recall, and match accuracy.
334	
335	**`answer_key.json` fields beyond the schema:** `id` (`<email>-<n>`); `qty_tol` (relative
336	tolerance on qty: `0` exact, `null` = unscored); `must_mention` (phrases the description must
337	contain; `"a|b"` = either; case, spaces and punctuation ignored, and common spellings of the
338	same spec count as equal — Sch/Schedule, 150#/150 lb/Class 150, BW/butt weld, threaded/NPT,
339	SMLS/seamless, galv/galvanized, and the catalog's abbreviations ELL, VLV, FLG, GSKT, SPW, MI,
340	CS, FP, RED, CPLG); `must_not_mention` (phrases
341	it must not contain — a default that this line overrides, or a note that belongs to another
342	section); `sku` / `match` / `candidates` (the catalog answer for the optional matcher).

344	#!/usr/bin/env python3
345	"""Validate the SHAPE of your parsed.json.  This checks structure only — it scores nothing.
346	
347	    python check_format.py parsed.json
348	    python check_format.py parsed.json --emails dev/emails     # also: every email appears
349	
350	Every problem is printed as <email>.<field> or <email>.line_items[i].<field>;
351	exit 0 = ok, 2 = shape problems, 1 = file missing or not JSON.  README.md defines each field.
352	"""
353	
354	from __future__ import annotations
355	
356	import argparse
357	import json
358	import sys
359	from pathlib import Path
360	
361	CLASSES = (
362	    "rfq",
363	    "rfq_revision",
364	    "purchase_order",
365	    "vendor_quote",
366	    "status_inquiry",
367	    "auto_reply",
368	    "other",
369	)
370	MATCHES = ("matched", "not_in_catalog", "ambiguous")
371	UOMS = ("EA", "FT", "M", "IN", "BX", "PK", "PR", "DZ", "RL", "LB", "SET", "GAL", "BAG", "CS")
372	
373	
374	def _num(x) -> bool:
375	    return isinstance(x, (int, float)) and not isinstance(x, bool)
376	
377	
378	def _str(x) -> bool:
379	    return isinstance(x, str) and bool(x.strip())
380	
381	
382	def check_line(w: str, ln) -> list[str]:
383	    if not isinstance(ln, dict):
384	        return [f"{w}: must be an object"]
385	    errs = []
386	    if not _str(ln.get("raw")):
387	        errs.append(f"{w}.raw: required — the line's text as it appears in the email or attachment")
388	    if not _str(ln.get("description")):
389	        errs.append(f"{w}.description: required — the item, self-contained, with its context")
390	    if "qty" not in ln:
391	        errs.append(f"{w}.qty: required (a number, or null when not stated)")
392	    elif ln["qty"] is not None and not _num(ln["qty"]):
393	        errs.append(f"{w}.qty: must be a number or null")
394	    if ln.get("uom") is not None and ln["uom"] not in UOMS:
395	        errs.append(f"{w}.uom: must be one of {list(UOMS)} or null")
396	    if not _str(ln.get("source")):
397	        errs.append(f"{w}.source: required — 'body' or the attachment's filename")
398	    if "match" in ln or "sku" in ln:  # optional matcher
399	        m = ln.get("match")
400	        if m not in MATCHES:
401	            errs.append(f"{w}.match: one of {list(MATCHES)} when you match (optional)")
402	        elif m == "matched" and not _str(ln.get("sku")):
403	            errs.append(f"{w}.sku: required when match is 'matched'")
404	        elif m != "matched" and ln.get("sku") is not None:
405	            errs.append(f"{w}.sku: must be null when match is '{m}'")
406	        if ln.get("candidates") is not None and not (
407	            isinstance(ln["candidates"], list) and all(_str(c) for c in ln["candidates"])
408	        ):
409	            errs.append(f"{w}.candidates: a list of skus")
410	    return errs
411	
412	
413	def check(data) -> list[str]:
414	    if not isinstance(data, dict):
415	        return ['parsed.json must be a JSON object keyed by email id (e.g. "E001")']
416	    errs = []
417	    for eid, v in data.items():
418	        if not isinstance(v, dict):
419	            errs.append(f"{eid}: must be an object")
420	            continue
421	        if v.get("classification") not in CLASSES:
422	            errs.append(f"{eid}.classification: must be one of {list(CLASSES)}")
423	        for f in ("revises", "duplicate_of"):
424	            if v.get(f) is not None and not _str(v[f]):
425	                errs.append(f"{eid}.{f}: must be an email id string or null")
426	        if not isinstance(v.get("needs_review"), bool):
427	            errs.append(f"{eid}.needs_review: required, true or false")
428	        if v.get("needs_review") and not _str(v.get("review_reason")):
429	            errs.append(f"{eid}.review_reason: required when needs_review is true")
430	        lines = v.get("line_items")
431	        if not isinstance(lines, list):
432	            errs.append(f"{eid}.line_items: required, a list ([] when there is nothing to extract)")
433	            continue
434	        for i, ln in enumerate(lines):
435	            errs += check_line(f"{eid}.line_items[{i}]", ln)
436	    return errs

466	"""Optional helper: .eml -> JSON + attachment files.  Use it, port it, or ignore it.  Stdlib only.
467	
468	    python eml_to_json.py dev/emails/E001.eml                      # one email -> stdout
469	    python eml_to_json.py dev/emails --out inbox.json --files att  # all emails; attachments saved
470	
471	Shape: {id, headers{from,to,cc,date,subject,message_id,in_reply_to,references},
472	        text, html, attachments:[{filename, mime, size, inline, content_id, path}]}
473	`path` is set only with --files (bytes written to <files>/<id>/<filename>).  A forwarded or
474	bounced message attached as message/rfc822 is saved as a .eml file.  Reading what is INSIDE an
475	attachment (Excel, PDF, scans, photos ...) is up to you.
476	"""
477	
478	from __future__ import annotations
479	
480	import argparse
481	import json
482	import re
483	import sys
484	from email import policy
485	from email.parser import BytesParser
486	from pathlib import Path
487	
488	HEADERS = ("from", "to", "cc", "date", "subject", "message-id", "in-reply-to", "references")
489	
490	
491	def _text(part) -> str:
492	    try:
493	        return part.get_content()
494	    except Exception:  # unknown charset / bad transfer encoding
495	        return (part.get_payload(decode=True) or b"").decode("utf-8", "replace")
496	
497	
498	def _safe(name: str) -> str:
499	    return re.sub(r"[^\w.\- ]+", "_", name).strip() or "unnamed"
500	
501	
502	def eml_to_json(path: Path, files: Path | None = None) -> dict:
503	    msg = BytesParser(policy=policy.default).parsebytes(path.read_bytes())
504	    out = {
505	        "id": path.stem,
506	        "headers": {h.replace("-", "_"): msg.get(h) for h in HEADERS},
507	        "text": None,
508	        "html": None,
509	        "attachments": [],
510	    }
511	    stack = [msg]
512	    while stack:
513	        part = stack.pop(0)
514	        ct = part.get_content_type()
515	        if ct == "message/rfc822":
516	            data = (
517	                part.get_payload(0).as_bytes()
518	                if part.is_multipart()
519	                else part.get_payload(decode=True)
520	            )
521	            _add(out, part, data, files, default=f"attached-{len(out['attachments']) + 1}.eml")
522	            continue
523	        if part.is_multipart():
524	            stack[0:0] = list(part.iter_parts())
525	            continue
526	        disp = part.get_content_disposition()
527	        if disp in ("attachment", "inline") and (part.get_filename() or ct.split("/")[0] != "text"):
528	            _add(out, part, part.get_payload(decode=True) or b"", files)
529	        elif ct == "text/plain" and out["text"] is None:
530	            out["text"] = _text(part)
531	        elif ct == "text/html" and out["html"] is None:
532	            out["html"] = _text(part)
533	    return out

535	
536	def _add(out, part, data: bytes, files: Path | None, default: str = "unnamed") -> None:
537	    name = part.get_filename() or default
538	    item = {
539	        "filename": name,
540	        "mime": part.get_content_type(),
541	        "size": len(data),
542	        "inline": part.get_content_disposition() == "inline",
543	        "content_id": (part.get("Content-ID") or "").strip("<>") or None,
544	        "path": None,
545	    }
546	    if files:
547	        p = files / out["id"] / _safe(name)
548	        p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
549	        p.write_bytes(data)
550	        item["path"] = str(p)
551	    out["attachments"].append(item)

555	    sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")
556	    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawTextHelpFormatter)
557	    ap.add_argument("path", type=Path, help=".eml file or a directory of them")
558	    ap.add_argument("--out", type=Path, help="write JSON here instead of stdout")
559	    ap.add_argument("--files", type=Path, help="save attachment bytes under this directory")
560	    a = ap.parse_args(argv)
561	    if a.path.is_dir():
562	        data = {p.stem: eml_to_json(p, a.files) for p in sorted(a.path.glob("*.eml"))}
563	    else:

566	    if a.out:
567	        a.out.write_text(s + "\n", encoding="utf-8")

12	# The RFQ Inbox — a four-day problem
13	
14	> Read *The situation*, then open the twenty-four dev emails, then come back for the rest. This
15	> document is short on purpose: most of what matters here is *your* judgment, not ours.

17	## The situation
18	
19	You have just joined **Ridgeline Industrial Supply**, a distributor of pipe, fittings, flanges,
20	valves and bolting. Ridgeline's inside sales reps spend most of their day on one inbox:
21	customers asking for prices. On a good day that is a tidy list in the body of an email. Most
22	days it's a spreadsheet with "ALL PIPE SCH 40" in a merged cell above the rows that need it, a
23	phone photo of a list a foreman wrote on a clipboard, a scan of a scan, a reply that says
24	"make #3 twelve and kill #5" to an email from last week, a supplier's quote that looks exactly
25	like a customer's request, and a bounce notification with somebody's whole order attached.
26	
27	Every one of those has to become a clean list of what the customer wants — or a flag saying a
28	human needs to look — before anyone can quote it. A missed email is a customer who never
29	hears back. A line read wrong is a wrong quote.
30	
31	**Your job: build the thing that reads this inbox.** For every email, decide what kind of email
32	it is, and pull out exactly the items being asked for, each one self-contained — with the
33	schedule, material or rating that the customer wrote somewhere *other* than on that line.
34	
35	You will need a model to do it — several of these emails are photos and scans, and most of
36	the rest hide their meaning in headings, notes and threads. Calling a model is the easy part.
37	What we are assessing is **how you put it to work**: what it decides and what your code checks,
38	how you know it's right, what it costs, and what happens when it's wrong, slow, or down.

212	## parsed.json
213	
214	One object keyed by the `.eml` filename stem. **Every email in the directory must appear.**
215	
216	```json
217	{
218	  "E003": {
219	    "classification": "rfq",
220	    "revises": null,
221	    "duplicate_of": null,
222	    "needs_review": false,
223	    "review_reason": null,
224	    "line_items": [
225	      {
226	        "raw": "2\" x 21' - 12 lengths",
227	        "description": "2\" pipe, SCH 40 A53B ERW, threaded & coupled, 21' lengths",
228	        "qty": 12,
229	        "uom": "EA",
230	        "source": "body"
231	      }
232	    ]
233	  }
234	}
235	```
236	
237	### classification — exactly one per email
238	
239	| value | the **current** message … | line_items |
240	|---|---|---|
241	| `rfq` | asks us to price or check availability of items | the items |
242	| `rfq_revision` | changes a request made earlier in the same thread (quantities, additions, removals) | the **complete** order as now intended; `revises` = the earlier email's id if it is in the inbox, else null |
243	| `purchase_order` | commits to buy — a PO, "please process", "go ahead with items 1–3" | the items ordered |
244	| `vendor_quote` | is a supplier quoting or answering **us** | `[]` |
245	| `status_inquiry` | asks about an existing quote or order (update? ETA? tracking?) | `[]` |
246	| `auto_reply` | is machine-generated: out-of-office, bounce, receipt | `[]` |
247	| `other` | anything else: marketing, invoices and remittances, job applications, internal chatter, "we went with someone else" | `[]` |
248	
249	Classify what the current message *does* — not the subject line, not the quoted history.
250	
251	### line_items — one per thing the customer is asking for
252	
253	- **What counts.** Items in the current message, its attachments and pasted pictures, and —
254	  when one of our own reps forwards a customer's email — in the forwarded content. Not items
255	  in quoted earlier messages (they were handled when they arrived), not headings, notes,
256	  totals, prices, signatures, crossed-out lines, or old revisions of a document.
257	- **`raw`** — the line's text as it appears where you found it (a table row's cells on one
258	  line; for a picture or scan, your reading of it). We pair your lines with ours on these
259	  tokens, so keep it close to the source.
260	- **`description`** — the item **self-contained**, as an ISR would type it into a quote
261	  without re-reading the email: the line's own words plus every heading, note, column
262	  header, sheet name, form field, subject line or earlier line that applies to it — and
263	  nothing that doesn't apply to it. Never invent a spec the email doesn't give.
264	- **`qty` / `uom`** — as the customer stated it, not converted. A number spelled out is a
265	  number; a vague amount ("a couple", "enough for the job") is `null`. A size, schedule,
266	  length, rating, part number or price is never a quantity. `uom` is one of `EA FT M IN BX
267	  PK PR DZ RL LB SET GAL BAG CS`, or `null` when no unit is stated (we read `null` as `EA`).
268	- **`source`** — `"body"`, or the filename of the attachment / pasted image the line came from.
269	
270	### Threads, duplicates, forwards
271	
272	- A reply that changes an earlier request → `rfq_revision` with the **complete** order as the
273	  customer now intends it; the earlier email keeps its own lines as they were on arrival.
274	- The same request sent twice → **the email with the later `Date:` is the duplicate**: same
275	  classification as the original, `duplicate_of` = the original's id, `line_items: []`.
276	- Anything **from** `@ridgeline-supply.example` is one of our own reps, usually forwarding a
277	  customer's email; classify it as the customer's email, and read the rep's own note too.
278	
279	### needs_review — "a human has to look at this before anyone quotes it"
280	
281	`true` when the email asks for something you cannot fully read or resolve: the attachment it
282	points at is missing or can't be opened, or the items themselves are only identified by
283	something that isn't in the email ("same as our last order, but double it"). Put the reason in `review_reason` (required when `true`) and still
284	return whatever lines you *could* read. Only for `rfq`, `rfq_revision` and `purchase_order`.
285	
286	## Optional: matching to the catalog
287	
288	If you build the optional matcher, add three fields to each line item:
289	
290	```json
291	{"raw": "...", "description": "...", "qty": 12, "uom": "EA", "source": "body",
292	 "sku": "RL-12345", "match": "matched", "match_reason": "2\" 150# RF weld neck A105: one part fits"}
293	```
294	
295	- `match` is one of `matched` (exactly one catalog part is what the customer asked for —
296	  `sku` is it), `not_in_catalog` (we don't stock it — `sku: null`), or `ambiguous` (more than
297	  one stocked part fits what the customer wrote and they'd have to choose — `sku: null`,
298	  optional `candidates: [skus]`).
299	- `match_reason` — one short line a rep can check.
300	- **Not in catalog is a decision, not a failure.** Ridgeline doesn't stock everything
301	  customers ask for, and the nearest catalog part is often one attribute away — right size and
302	  type, wrong schedule, rating or material. Quoting that part is a wrong quote.
303	- `catalog.csv` columns: `sku, description, category, product, size, spec` (schedule or
304	  pressure class)`, material, ends, extra, uom`. Descriptions are abbreviated the way an ERP
305	  prints them.
306	
307	## World facts
308	
309	- Ridgeline Industrial Supply sells pipe, fittings, flanges, valves, gaskets, bolting and
310	  related industrial supplies. The RFQ inbox is `rfq@ridgeline-supply.example`.
311	- Our quotes are numbered `Q-26-…`. Customers' RFQ and PO numbers are theirs.
312	- A supplier answering *our* request for pricing is a `vendor_quote`, however much it looks
313	  like a list of items.
314	
315	## What we grade
316	
317	Your `parse` command on the held-out inbox, against our key, **before we read anything you wrote**.
318	
319	**Headline numbers** — the expensive failures, in this order:
320	1. **Silent losses** — an email that needed someone to act (it has items, or needs review)
321	   came back with no lines and no review flag. That customer never hears back.
322	2. **Hallucinated lines** — lines that aren't requests: quoted history, headings, prices,
323	   signatures, crossed-out or superseded rows.
324	3. **Lost and phantom requests** — a request classified as something else (lost), or a
325	   vendor quote / bounce / newsletter classified as a request (phantom).
326	
327	Then: classification accuracy, line recall and precision, and on paired lines — `qty`,
328	`uom`, `source`, and **context carried** (does the `description` mention what the key's
329	`must_mention` lists, and none of its `must_not_mention`?). Plus `revises` / `duplicate_of`
330	links and `needs_review` precision/recall.
331	
332	**Optional matcher**, if present: confident wrong matches (you named a part; the answer was a
333	different part, *not in catalog*, or *ambiguous*), not-in-catalog recall, and match accuracy.
334	
335	**`answer_key.json` fields beyond the schema:** `id` (`<email>-<n>`); `qty_tol` (relative
336	tolerance on qty: `0` exact, `null` = unscored); `must_mention` (phrases the description must
337	contain; `"a|b"` = either; case, spaces and punctuation ignored, and common spellings of the
338	same spec count as equal — Sch/Schedule, 150#/150 lb/Class 150, BW/butt weld, threaded/NPT,
339	SMLS/seamless, galv/galvanized, and the catalog's abbreviations ELL, VLV, FLG, GSKT, SPW, MI,
340	CS, FP, RED, CPLG); `must_not_mention` (phrases
341	it must not contain — a default that this line overrides, or a note that belongs to another
342	section); `sku` / `match` / `candidates` (the catalog answer for the optional matcher).
343	----
344	#!/usr/bin/env python3
345	"""Validate the SHAPE of your parsed.json.  This checks structure only — it scores nothing.
346	
347	    python check_format.py parsed.json
348	    python check_format.py parsed.json --emails dev/emails     # also: every email appears
349	
350	Every problem is printed as <email>.<field> or <email>.line_items[i].<field>;
351	exit 0 = ok, 2 = shape problems, 1 = file missing or not JSON.  README.md defines each field.
352	"""
353	
354	from __future__ import annotations
355	
356	import argparse
357	import json
358	import sys
359	from pathlib import Path
360	
361	CLASSES = (
362	    "rfq",
363	    "rfq_revision",
364	    "purchase_order",
365	    "vendor_quote",
366	    "status_inquiry",
367	    "auto_reply",
368	    "other",
369	)
370	MATCHES = ("matched", "not_in_catalog", "ambiguous")
371	UOMS = ("EA", "FT", "M", "IN", "BX", "PK", "PR", "DZ", "RL", "LB", "SET", "GAL", "BAG", "CS")
372	
373	
374	def _num(x) -> bool:
375	    return isinstance(x, (int, float)) and not isinstance(x, bool)
376	
377	
378	def _str(x) -> bool:
379	    return isinstance(x, str) and bool(x.strip())
380	
381	
382	def check_line(w: str, ln) -> list[str]:
383	    if not isinstance(ln, dict):
384	        return [f"{w}: must be an object"]
385	    errs = []
386	    if not _str(ln.get("raw")):
387	        errs.append(f"{w}.raw: required — the line's text as it appears in the email or attachment")
388	    if not _str(ln.get("description")):
389	        errs.append(f"{w}.description: required — the item, self-contained, with its context")
390	    if "qty" not in ln:
391	        errs.append(f"{w}.qty: required (a number, or null when not stated)")
392	    elif ln["qty"] is not None and not _num(ln["qty"]):
393	        errs.append(f"{w}.qty: must be a number or null")
394	    if ln.get("uom") is not None and ln["uom"] not in UOMS:
395	        errs.append(f"{w}.uom: must be one of {list(UOMS)} or null")
396	    if not _str(ln.get("source")):
397	        errs.append(f"{w}.source: required — 'body' or the attachment's filename")
398	    if "match" in ln or "sku" in ln:  # optional matcher
399	        m = ln.get("match")
400	        if m not in MATCHES:
401	            errs.append(f"{w}.match: one of {list(MATCHES)} when you match (optional)")
402	        elif m == "matched" and not _str(ln.get("sku")):
403	            errs.append(f"{w}.sku: required when match is 'matched'")
404	        elif m != "matched" and ln.get("sku") is not None:
405	            errs.append(f"{w}.sku: must be null when match is '{m}'")
406	        if ln.get("candidates") is not None and not (
407	            isinstance(ln["candidates"], list) and all(_str(c) for c in ln["candidates"])
408	        ):
409	            errs.append(f"{w}.candidates: a list of skus")
410	    return errs
411	
412	
413	def check(data) -> list[str]:
414	    if not isinstance(data, dict):
415	        return ['parsed.json must be a JSON object keyed by email id (e.g. "E001")']
416	    errs = []
417	    for eid, v in data.items():
418	        if not isinstance(v, dict):
419	            errs.append(f"{eid}: must be an object")
420	            continue
421	        if v.get("classification") not in CLASSES:
422	            errs.append(f"{eid}.classification: must be one of {list(CLASSES)}")
423	        for f in ("revises", "duplicate_of"):
424	            if v.get(f) is not None and not _str(v[f]):
425	                errs.append(f"{eid}.{f}: must be an email id string or null")
426	        if not isinstance(v.get("needs_review"), bool):
427	            errs.append(f"{eid}.needs_review: required, true or false")
428	        if v.get("needs_review") and not _str(v.get("review_reason")):
429	            errs.append(f"{eid}.review_reason: required when needs_review is true")
430	        lines = v.get("line_items")
431	        if not isinstance(lines, list):
432	            errs.append(f"{eid}.line_items: required, a list ([] when there is nothing to extract)")
433	            continue
434	        for i, ln in enumerate(lines):
435	            errs += check_line(f"{eid}.line_items[{i}]", ln)
436	    return errs
437	
438	
439	def main(argv=None) -> int:
440	    sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")
441	    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawTextHelpFormatter)
442	    ap.add_argument("parsed", type=Path)
443	    ap.add_argument("--emails", type=Path, help="directory of .eml files that must all appear")
444	    a = ap.parse_args(argv)
445	    try:
446	        data = json.loads(a.parsed.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
447	    except (OSError, ValueError) as e:
448	        print(f"{a.parsed}: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
449	        return 1
450	    errs = check(data)
451	    if a.emails:
452	        want = {p.stem for p in a.emails.glob("*.eml")}
453	        errs += [
454	            f"{eid}: missing (every email in {a.emails} must appear)"
455	            for eid in sorted(want - set(data))
456	        ]
457	    for e in errs:
458	        print(e)
459	    print(f"{len(data) if isinstance(data, dict) else 0} emails, {len(errs)} problem(s)")
460	    return 2 if errs else 0
461	
462	
463	if __name__ == "__main__":
464	    sys.exit(main())

466	"""Optional helper: .eml -> JSON + attachment files.  Use it, port it, or ignore it.  Stdlib only.
467	
468	    python eml_to_json.py dev/emails/E001.eml                      # one email -> stdout
469	    python eml_to_json.py dev/emails --out inbox.json --files att  # all emails; attachments saved
470	
471	Shape: {id, headers{from,to,cc,date,subject,message_id,in_reply_to,references},
472	        text, html, attachments:[{filename, mime, size, inline, content_id, path}]}
473	`path` is set only with --files (bytes written to <files>/<id>/<filename>).  A forwarded or
474	bounced message attached as message/rfc822 is saved as a .eml file.  Reading what is INSIDE an
475	attachment (Excel, PDF, scans, photos ...) is up to you.
476	"""
477	
478	from __future__ import annotations
479	
480	import argparse
481	import json
482	import re
483	import sys
484	from email import policy
485	from email.parser import BytesParser
486	from pathlib import Path
487	
488	HEADERS = ("from", "to", "cc", "date", "subject", "message-id", "in-reply-to", "references")
489	
490	
491	def _text(part) -> str:
492	    try:
493	        return part.get_content()
494	    except Exception:  # unknown charset / bad transfer encoding
495	        return (part.get_payload(decode=True) or b"").decode("utf-8", "replace")
496	
497	
498	def _safe(name: str) -> str:
499	    return re.sub(r"[^\w.\- ]+", "_", name).strip() or "unnamed"
500	
501	
502	def eml_to_json(path: Path, files: Path | None = None) -> dict:
503	    msg = BytesParser(policy=policy.default).parsebytes(path.read_bytes())
504	    out = {
505	        "id": path.stem,
506	        "headers": {h.replace("-", "_"): msg.get(h) for h in HEADERS},
507	        "text": None,
508	        "html": None,
509	        "attachments": [],
510	    }
511	    stack = [msg]
512	    while stack:
513	        part = stack.pop(0)
514	        ct = part.get_content_type()
515	        if ct == "message/rfc822":
516	            data = (
517	                part.get_payload(0).as_bytes()
518	                if part.is_multipart()
519	                else part.get_payload(decode=True)
520	            )
521	            _add(out, part, data, files, default=f"attached-{len(out['attachments']) + 1}.eml")
522	            continue
523	        if part.is_multipart():
524	            stack[0:0] = list(part.iter_parts())
525	            continue
526	        disp = part.get_content_disposition()
527	        if disp in ("attachment", "inline") and (part.get_filename() or ct.split("/")[0] != "text"):
528	            _add(out, part, part.get_payload(decode=True) or b"", files)
529	        elif ct == "text/plain" and out["text"] is None:
530	            out["text"] = _text(part)
531	        elif ct == "text/html" and out["html"] is None:
532	            out["html"] = _text(part)
533	    return out
534	
535	
536	def _add(out, part, data: bytes, files: Path | None, default: str = "unnamed") -> None:
537	    name = part.get_filename() or default
538	    item = {
539	        "filename": name,
540	        "mime": part.get_content_type(),
541	        "size": len(data),
542	        "inline": part.get_content_disposition() == "inline",
543	        "content_id": (part.get("Content-ID") or "").strip("<>") or None,
544	        "path": None,
545	    }
546	    if files:
547	        p = files / out["id"] / _safe(name)
548	        p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
549	        p.write_bytes(data)
550	        item["path"] = str(p)
551	    out["attachments"].append(item)
552	
553	
554	def main(argv=None) -> int:
555	    sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")
556	    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawTextHelpFormatter)
557	    ap.add_argument("path", type=Path, help=".eml file or a directory of them")
558	    ap.add_argument("--out", type=Path, help="write JSON here instead of stdout")
559	    ap.add_argument("--files", type=Path, help="save attachment bytes under this directory")
560	    a = ap.parse_args(argv)
561	    if a.path.is_dir():
562	        data = {p.stem: eml_to_json(p, a.files) for p in sorted(a.path.glob("*.eml"))}
563	    else:
564	        data = eml_to_json(a.path, a.files)
565	    s = json.dumps(data, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
566	    if a.out:
567	        a.out.write_text(s + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
568	    else:
569	        print(s)
570	    return 0
571	
572	
573	if __name__ == "__main__":
574	    sys.exit(main())

# The RFQ Inbox — a four-day problem

> Read *The situation*, then open the twenty-four dev emails, then come back for the rest. This
> document is short on purpose: most of what matters here is *your* judgment, not ours.

## The situation

You have just joined **Ridgeline Industrial Supply**, a distributor of pipe, fittings, flanges,
valves and bolting. Ridgeline's inside sales reps spend most of their day on one inbox:
customers asking for prices. On a good day that is a tidy list in the body of an email. Most
days it's a spreadsheet with "ALL PIPE SCH 40" in a merged cell above the rows that need it, a
phone photo of a list a foreman wrote on a clipboard, a scan of a scan, a reply that says
"make #3 twelve and kill #5" to an email from last week, a supplier's quote that looks exactly
like a customer's request, and a bounce notification with somebody's whole order attached.

Every one of those has to become a clean list of what the customer wants — or a flag saying a
human needs to look — before anyone can quote it. A missed email is a customer who never
hears back. A line read wrong is a wrong quote.

**Your job: build the thing that reads this inbox.** For every email, decide what kind of email
it is, and pull out exactly the items being asked for, each one self-contained — with the
schedule, material or rating that the customer wrote somewhere *other* than on that line.

You will need a model to do it — several of these emails are photos and scans, and most of
the rest hide their meaning in headings, notes and threads. Calling a model is the easy part.
What we are assessing is **how you put it to work**: what it decides and what your code checks,
how you know it's right, what it costs, and what happens when it's wrong, slow, or down.

## What you are given

```
data/
  README.md            the contract: the command, the output format, how we grade — read it in full
  eml_to_json.py       optional helper: .eml → JSON + the attachment files
  check_format.py      validates your output's shape (it scores nothing)
  catalog.csv          what Ridgeline stocks — for the optional matcher
  dev/
    emails/*.eml       24 inbox emails
    answer_key.json    what a careful rep made of each one — your ground truth
```

There is also a **held-out inbox** of ~40 emails from the same company — the same kinds of
customers, documents and surprises, none of the same strings, and a few situations dev doesn't
show you. We run your submission against it. Work that passes dev by fitting it will not
survive that; work built from understanding *why* dev is hard will. All data is synthetic.

## What to build

One command, exactly as `data/README.md` defines it:

```
parse --emails <dir> --out parsed.json
```

Per email: a **classification** (seven kinds), the **line items** (verbatim text,
self-contained description, quantity, unit, where it came from), and a **needs-review** flag
for when you can't — or shouldn't — answer alone.

**Build it like it will run on the real inbox tomorrow.** Four properties are required, and we
test each of them:

1. **Replayable.** On the dev inbox it runs with **no API key** — record or cache model
   responses and commit them.
2. **Idempotent and cheap to re-run.** Running it twice on the same inbox makes no new model
   calls the second time.
3. **One bad email never takes down the run.** Some attachments are broken on purpose; some
   things are unreadable for anyone. Those come back flagged, and the run carries on.
4. **You know what it cost.** Tell us the model calls, tokens and dollars per email on dev.

## Optional — if you have time left

Never required, never penalised when skipped. If you build the matcher we run its numbers too,
but both parts are weighed in the interview, not in your score. Both are good places to show
judgment the core can't.

- **The matcher, designed (and built if you like).** Each extracted line eventually has to
  become a catalog part — or a decision that Ridgeline doesn't stock it. The catalog does not
  carry everything customers ask for, and the closest part is often one attribute off (right

## parsed.json

One object keyed by the `.eml` filename stem. **Every email in the directory must appear.**

```json
{
  "E003": {
    "classification": "rfq",
    "revises": null,
    "duplicate_of": null,
    "needs_review": false,
    "review_reason": null,
    "line_items": [
      {
        "raw": "2\" x 21' - 12 lengths",
        "description": "2\" pipe, SCH 40 A53B ERW, threaded & coupled, 21' lengths",
        "qty": 12,
        "uom": "EA",
        "source": "body"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

### classification — exactly one per email

| value | the **current** message … | line_items |
|---|---|---|
| `rfq` | asks us to price or check availability of items | the items |
| `rfq_revision` | changes a request made earlier in the same thread (quantities, additions, removals) | the **complete** order as now intended; `revises` = the earlier email's id if it is in the inbox, else null |
| `purchase_order` | commits to buy — a PO, "please process", "go ahead with items 1–3" | the items ordered |
| `vendor_quote` | is a supplier quoting or answering **us** | `[]` |
| `status_inquiry` | asks about an existing quote or order (update? ETA? tracking?) | `[]` |
| `auto_reply` | is machine-generated: out-of-office, bounce, receipt | `[]` |
| `other` | anything else: marketing, invoices and remittances, job applications, internal chatter, "we went with someone else" | `[]` |

Classify what the current message *does* — not the subject line, not the quoted history.

### line_items — one per thing the customer is asking for

- **What counts.** Items in the current message, its attachments and pasted pictures, and —
  when one of our own reps forwards a customer's email — in the forwarded content. Not items
  in quoted earlier messages (they were handled when they arrived), not headings, notes,
  totals, prices, signatures, crossed-out lines, or old revisions of a document.
- **`raw`** — the line's text as it appears where you found it (a table row's cells on one
  line; for a picture or scan, your reading of it). We pair your lines with ours on these
  tokens, so keep it close to the source.
- **`description`** — the item **self-contained**, as an ISR would type it into a quote
  without re-reading the email: the line's own words plus every heading, note, column
  header, sheet name, form field, subject line or earlier line that applies to it — and
  nothing that doesn't apply to it. Never invent a spec the email doesn't give.
- **`qty` / `uom`** — as the customer stated it, not converted. A number spelled out is a
  number; a vague amount ("a couple", "enough for the job") is `null`. A size, schedule,
  length, rating, part number or price is never a quantity. `uom` is one of `EA FT M IN BX
  PK PR DZ RL LB SET GAL BAG CS`, or `null` when no unit is stated (we read `null` as `EA`).
- **`source`** — `"body"`, or the filename of the attachment / pasted image the line came from.

### Threads, duplicates, forwards

- A reply that changes an earlier request → `rfq_revision` with the **complete** order as the
  customer now intends it; the earlier email keeps its own lines as they were on arrival.
- The same request sent twice → **the email with the later `Date:` is the duplicate**: same
  classification as the original, `duplicate_of` = the original's id, `line_items: []`.
- Anything **from** `@ridgeline-supply.example` is one of our own reps, usually forwarding a
  customer's email; classify it as the customer's email, and read the rep's own note too.

### needs_review — "a human has to look at this before anyone quotes it"

`true` when the email asks for something you cannot fully read or resolve: the attachment it
points at is missing or can't be opened, or the items themselves are only identified by
something that isn't in the email ("same as our last order, but double it"). Put the reason in `review_reason` (required when `true`) and still
return whatever lines you *could* read. Only for `rfq`, `rfq_revision` and `purchase_order`.

## Optional: matching to the catalog

If you build the optional matcher, add three fields to each line item:

```json
{"raw": "...", "description": "...", "qty": 12, "uom": "EA", "source": "body",
 "sku": "RL-12345", "match": "matched", "match_reason": "2\" 150# RF weld neck A105: one part fits"}
```

- `match` is one of `matched` (exactly one catalog part is what the customer asked for —
  `sku` is it), `not_in_catalog` (we don't stock it — `sku: null`), or `ambiguous` (more than
  one stocked part fits what the customer wrote and they'd have to choose — `sku: null`,
  optional `candidates: [skus]`).
- `match_reason` — one short line a rep can check.
- **Not in catalog is a decision, not a failure.** Ridgeline doesn't stock everything
  customers ask for, and the nearest catalog part is often one attribute away — right size and
  type, wrong schedule, rating or material. Quoting that part is a wrong quote.
- `catalog.csv` columns: `sku, description, category, product, size, spec` (schedule or
  pressure class)`, material, ends, extra, uom`. Descriptions are abbreviated the way an ERP
  prints them.

## World facts

- Ridgeline Industrial Supply sells pipe, fittings, flanges, valves, gaskets, bolting and
  related industrial supplies. The RFQ inbox is `rfq@ridgeline-supply.example`.
- Our quotes are numbered `Q-26-…`. Customers' RFQ and PO numbers are theirs.
- A supplier answering *our* request for pricing is a `vendor_quote`, however much it looks
  like a list of items.

## What we grade

Your `parse` command on the held-out inbox, against our key, **before we read anything you wrote**.

**Headline numbers** — the expensive failures, in this order:
1. **Silent losses** — an email that needed someone to act (it has items, or needs review)
   came back with no lines and no review flag. That customer never hears back.
2. **Hallucinated lines** — lines that aren't requests: quoted history, headings, prices,
   signatures, crossed-out or superseded rows.
3. **Lost and phantom requests** — a request classified as something else (lost), or a
   vendor quote / bounce / newsletter classified as a request (phantom).

Then: classification accuracy, line recall and precision, and on paired lines — `qty`,
`uom`, `source`, and **context carried** (does the `description` mention what the key's
`must_mention` lists, and none of its `must_not_mention`?). Plus `revises` / `duplicate_of`
links and `needs_review` precision/recall.

**Optional matcher**, if present: confident wrong matches (you named a part; the answer was a
different part, *not in catalog*, or *ambiguous*), not-in-catalog recall, and match accuracy.

**`answer_key.json` fields beyond the schema:** `id` (`<email>-<n>`); `qty_tol` (relative
tolerance on qty: `0` exact, `null` = unscored); `must_mention` (phrases the description must
contain; `"a|b"` = either; case, spaces and punctuation ignored, and common spellings of the
same spec count as equal — Sch/Schedule, 150#/150 lb/Class 150, BW/butt weld, threaded/NPT,
SMLS/seamless, galv/galvanized, and the catalog's abbreviations ELL, VLV, FLG, GSKT, SPW, MI,
CS, FP, RED, CPLG); `must_not_mention` (phrases
it must not contain — a default that this line overrides, or a note that belongs to another
section); `sku` / `match` / `candidates` (the catalog answer for the optional matcher).

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Validate the SHAPE of your parsed.json.  This checks structure only — it scores nothing.

    python check_format.py parsed.json
    python check_format.py parsed.json --emails dev/emails     # also: every email appears

Every problem is printed as <email>.<field> or <email>.line_items[i].<field>;
exit 0 = ok, 2 = shape problems, 1 = file missing or not JSON.  README.md defines each field.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

CLASSES = (
    "rfq",
    "rfq_revision",
    "purchase_order",
    "vendor_quote",
    "status_inquiry",
    "auto_reply",
    "other",
)
MATCHES = ("matched", "not_in_catalog", "ambiguous")
UOMS = ("EA", "FT", "M", "IN", "BX", "PK", "PR", "DZ", "RL", "LB", "SET", "GAL", "BAG", "CS")


def _num(x) -> bool:
    return isinstance(x, (int, float)) and not isinstance(x, bool)


def _str(x) -> bool:
    return isinstance(x, str) and bool(x.strip())


def check_line(w: str, ln) -> list[str]:
    if not isinstance(ln, dict):
        return [f"{w}: must be an object"]
    errs = []
    if not _str(ln.get("raw")):
        errs.append(f"{w}.raw: required — the line's text as it appears in the email or attachment")
    if not _str(ln.get("description")):
        errs.append(f"{w}.description: required — the item, self-contained, with its context")
    if "qty" not in ln:
        errs.append(f"{w}.qty: required (a number, or null when not stated)")
    elif ln["qty"] is not None and not _num(ln["qty"]):
        errs.append(f"{w}.qty: must be a number or null")
    if ln.get("uom") is not None and ln["uom"] not in UOMS:
        errs.append(f"{w}.uom: must be one of {list(UOMS)} or null")
    if not _str(ln.get("source")):
        errs.append(f"{w}.source: required — 'body' or the attachment's filename")
    if "match" in ln or "sku" in ln:  # optional matcher
        m = ln.get("match")
        if m not in MATCHES:
            errs.append(f"{w}.match: one of {list(MATCHES)} when you match (optional)")
        elif m == "matched" and not _str(ln.get("sku")):
            errs.append(f"{w}.sku: required when match is 'matched'")
        elif m != "matched" and ln.get("sku") is not None:
            errs.append(f"{w}.sku: must be null when match is '{m}'")
        if ln.get("candidates") is not None and not (
            isinstance(ln["candidates"], list) and all(_str(c) for c in ln["candidates"])
        ):
            errs.append(f"{w}.candidates: a list of skus")
    return errs


def check(data) -> list[str]:
    if not isinstance(data, dict):
        return ['parsed.json must be a JSON object keyed by email id (e.g. "E001")']
    errs = []
    for eid, v in data.items():
        if not isinstance(v, dict):
            errs.append(f"{eid}: must be an object")
            continue
        if v.get("classification") not in CLASSES:
            errs.append(f"{eid}.classification: must be one of {list(CLASSES)}")
        for f in ("revises", "duplicate_of"):
            if v.get(f) is not None and not _str(v[f]):
                errs.append(f"{eid}.{f}: must be an email id string or null")
        if not isinstance(v.get("needs_review"), bool):
            errs.append(f"{eid}.needs_review: required, true or false")
        if v.get("needs_review") and not _str(v.get("review_reason")):
            errs.append(f"{eid}.review_reason: required when needs_review is true")
        lines = v.get("line_items")
        if not isinstance(lines, list):
            errs.append(f"{eid}.line_items: required, a list ([] when there is nothing to extract)")
            continue
        for i, ln in enumerate(lines):
            errs += check_line(f"{eid}.line_items[{i}]", ln)
    return errs


def main(argv=None) -> int:
    sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawTextHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("parsed", type=Path)
    ap.add_argument("--emails", type=Path, help="directory of .eml files that must all appear")
    a = ap.parse_args(argv)
    try:
        data = json.loads(a.parsed.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    except (OSError, ValueError) as e:
        print(f"{a.parsed}: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    errs = check(data)
    if a.emails:
        want = {p.stem for p in a.emails.glob("*.eml")}
        errs += [
            f"{eid}: missing (every email in {a.emails} must appear)"
            for eid in sorted(want - set(data))
        ]
    for e in errs:
        print(e)
    print(f"{len(data) if isinstance(data, dict) else 0} emails, {len(errs)} problem(s)")
    return 2 if errs else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Optional helper: .eml -> JSON + attachment files.  Use it, port it, or ignore it.  Stdlib only.

    python eml_to_json.py dev/emails/E001.eml                      # one email -> stdout
    python eml_to_json.py dev/emails --out inbox.json --files att  # all emails; attachments saved

Shape: {id, headers{from,to,cc,date,subject,message_id,in_reply_to,references},
        text, html, attachments:[{filename, mime, size, inline, content_id, path}]}
`path` is set only with --files (bytes written to <files>/<id>/<filename>).  A forwarded or
bounced message attached as message/rfc822 is saved as a .eml file.  Reading what is INSIDE an
attachment (Excel, PDF, scans, photos ...) is up to you.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import re
import sys
from email import policy
from email.parser import BytesParser
from pathlib import Path

HEADERS = ("from", "to", "cc", "date", "subject", "message-id", "in-reply-to", "references")


def _text(part) -> str:
    try:
        return part.get_content()
    except Exception:  # unknown charset / bad transfer encoding
        return (part.get_payload(decode=True) or b"").decode("utf-8", "replace")


def _safe(name: str) -> str:
    return re.sub(r"[^\w.\- ]+", "_", name).strip() or "unnamed"


def eml_to_json(path: Path, files: Path | None = None) -> dict:
    msg = BytesParser(policy=policy.default).parsebytes(path.read_bytes())
    out = {
        "id": path.stem,
        "headers": {h.replace("-", "_"): msg.get(h) for h in HEADERS},
        "text": None,
        "html": None,
        "attachments": [],
    }
    stack = [msg]
    while stack:
        part = stack.pop(0)
        ct = part.get_content_type()
        if ct == "message/rfc822":
            data = (
                part.get_payload(0).as_bytes()
                if part.is_multipart()
                else part.get_payload(decode=True)
            )
            _add(out, part, data, files, default=f"attached-{len(out['attachments']) + 1}.eml")
            continue
        if part.is_multipart():
            stack[0:0] = list(part.iter_parts())
            continue
        disp = part.get_content_disposition()
        if disp in ("attachment", "inline") and (part.get_filename() or ct.split("/")[0] != "text"):
            _add(out, part, part.get_payload(decode=True) or b"", files)
        elif ct == "text/plain" and out["text"] is None:
            out["text"] = _text(part)
        elif ct == "text/html" and out["html"] is None:
            out["html"] = _text(part)
    return out


def _add(out, part, data: bytes, files: Path | None, default: str = "unnamed") -> None:
    name = part.get_filename() or default
    item = {
        "filename": name,
        "mime": part.get_content_type(),
        "size": len(data),
        "inline": part.get_content_disposition() == "inline",
        "content_id": (part.get("Content-ID") or "").strip("<>") or None,
        "path": None,
    }
    if files:
        p = files / out["id"] / _safe(name)
        p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        p.write_bytes(data)
        item["path"] = str(p)
    out["attachments"].append(item)


def main(argv=None) -> int:
    sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawTextHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("path", type=Path, help=".eml file or a directory of them")
    ap.add_argument("--out", type=Path, help="write JSON here instead of stdout")
    ap.add_argument("--files", type=Path, help="save attachment bytes under this directory")
    a = ap.parse_args(argv)
    if a.path.is_dir():
        data = {p.stem: eml_to_json(p, a.files) for p in sorted(a.path.glob("*.eml"))}
    else:
        data = eml_to_json(a.path, a.files)
    s = json.dumps(data, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
    if a.out:
        a.out.write_text(s + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    else:
        print(s)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

content.text:
I read everything in `E:\candidate-package`: both docs, both scripts, the catalog, the answer key, all 24 emails and every attachment. The interruption was only because I'd unpacked the attachments to a folder that needed approval, so I moved them to the session scratchpad. Nothing in the project folder was changed.

## What this is
This is a take-home assessment. You have to build a `parse --emails <dir> --out parsed.json` command for Ridgeline Industrial Supply's quote-request inbox. For each email it gives a classification (one of 7 kinds), the line items, and a needs-review flag. It is run against about 40 unseen emails that you don't get. It's due **Sunday 15 Nov, 23:59 CST**, with a budget of 8–12 hours.

**The four hard requirements:**
- It runs on the dev inbox with no API key, using recorded model responses.
- A second run makes no model calls.
- One broken email never stops the run.
- It reports calls, tokens and dollars per email.

The default path has to use OpenAI.

**You also hand in:** `RUNNING.md`, `DECISIONS.md` (4 required sections), `AI_USAGE.md`, the raw `ai-sessions/` logs, a recording of 5 minutes or less, and real git history.

## What's in the folder
| File | Notes |
|---|---|
| `ASSESSMENT.md` | The brief |
| `data/README.md` | The output format and how it's graded. This is the real spec. |
| `data/eml_to_json.py` | Optional, standard library only. It unpacks MIME and saves attachments. |
| `data/check_format.py` | Checks the output's shape only, scores nothing |
| `data/catalog.csv` | 937 SKUs: 395 fittings, 178 pipe, 165 flanges, 121 valves, the rest gaskets, bolting and misc |
| `data/dev/answer_key.json` | Ground truth: 210 line items (194 matched to a catalog part, 16 not in the catalog) |
| `.idea/` | PyCharm project files only |

**Environment gaps:**
- This is not a git repo yet.
- Python is 3.14, with **no** openpyxl, pypdf, python-docx or PyMuPDF installed.

## The 24 emails and the trap in each
| Email | Answer key | What makes it hard |
|---|---|---|
| E001 | rfq, 5 lines | Clean baseline. The "Ref# 7/16-2211" looks like a size but isn't one. |
| E002 | rfq, 5 | Casual prose with no spec on the lines. Every line needs "316 threaded" from the subject line. "a couple caps" means qty = null. |
| E003 | rfq, 8 | Section headings set the spec. Pipe must not get "malleable/150#", and fittings must not get "SCH 40/A53B". |
| E004 | rfq_revision, revises E003 | "Line 2 is now 14, drop line 6, add 9". The output must be the complete merged order, rebuilt from the quoted E003. |
| E005 | rfq, from the xlsx | A merged cell says "ALL FITTINGS BW SCH 40 UNLESS NOTED". One line overrides it with SCH 80. There's a hidden "Rev A (old)" sheet and a TOTAL row, neither of which counts. |
| E006 | rfq, 44 | A 2-page text PDF. Material and rating sit in the form header. Two body lines are "also add" gaskets, which must not get A105. |
| E007 | rfq, 7 | Handwritten photo. One line is crossed out, and "„" ditto marks mean "same as the line above". |
| E008 | rfq, duplicate of E006, `[]` | A "RESEND" of the same PDF. The later date makes it the duplicate. |
| E009 | rfq, 32 | A tilted phone scan of a PDF form that runs over 2 pages, with section headings inside the table. |
| E010 | rfq, 6 | A screenshot of a pasted spreadsheet (image002). image001 is just a logo. |
| E011 | vendor_quote | A supplier answering our rep, with quantities and prices that look like a request. There's no In-Reply-To header. |
| E012 | status_inquiry | "Any update?" with a full quote request quoted below it. Extracting that quoted list would invent lines. |
| E013 | auto_reply | A bounce. The attached .eml is *our own* outgoing request to a vendor, not a customer's. |
| E014 | other | A supplier's sales email with a price table. |
| E015 | purchase_order, 6 | "Please process the attached PO." Prices and totals must not become lines. |
| E016 | rfq, 6 | Sent by our own rep (`@ridgeline-supply`), forwarding a customer's CSV. Classify it as the customer's email. |
| E017 | rfq, **needs_review**, 0 lines | "BOM attached", but the only attachment is the company's logo. The BOM is missing. |
| E018 | rfq, 6 | A table pasted into the body with one cell per line. The rows have to be rebuilt. "12 rolls" means uom = RL. |
| E019 | rfq, 9 | Word tables under headings. The fittings must not get "SCH 80 / A106" from the pipe heading. |
| E020 | purchase_order, 3 | "Go ahead with items 1, 2 and 4" of *our* quote, which is quoted below. The lines come from the quoted history, which breaks the usual rule. |
| E021 | rfq, 50 | Two sheets. The spec is only in the sheet names ("PIPE - SCH 80 SMLS", "FITTINGS - SW 3000#"). |
| E022 | rfq, **needs_review** | The PDF is encrypted, with "password to follow". |
| E023 | rfq, 1 | A photo of a valve nameplate. The line is built from the model number plus size, class, ends, body and trim. |
| E024 | rfq, 6 | Unicode ″ and ° symbols, and a spec heading above the table ("316 SS - THREADED - 3000#"). |

## Patterns that matter for the unseen emails
1. **Most of the difficulty is in carrying context.** Specs come from headings, sheet names, form headers, subject lines and "same size". The key's `must_not_mention` rules penalise putting a spec on a line it doesn't belong to (E003/E004, E005, E006, E019, E021).
2. **Quoted text is usually noise.** E012 and E004's own history should not be extracted. E020 is the exception, because the customer is choosing items from our quote.
3. **Who sent it decides the classification.** A vendor replying to us, a bounce of our own email, and our rep forwarding a customer all depend on the sender. Relying on headers alone fails, because E011 has no In-Reply-To.
4. **The worst failure is losing an email silently.** E017 and E022 have zero lines but must be flagged. "Attachment mentioned but unreadable or missing → needs_review" can be checked in code, not left to the model.
5. **Documents carry stale versions.** A hidden old revision, a crossed-out line and TOTAL rows all have to be left out.
6. **Matcher (optional):** the catalog does stock a Y-strainer and an eccentric reducer, but the key marks E016's and E018's as not in the catalog. That suggests the right type is in stock but one attribute is wrong, which is the "one attribute off" trap the brief describes.

## Where to push back in DECISIONS.md
- E020 goes against the README's "not items in quoted earlier messages" rule.
- The README defines needs_review, but the key has no `review_reason` text.
- E008 is graded as `rfq` with no lines rather than as its own kind of email, so a duplicate gets lines: [] even though it is a real request.

I can scaffold the project next: git init, the parse command layout, a response cache keyed by content hash, and the dependencies to install for xlsx, docx and pdf.

Pausing here. This is the plan in full, and where I am in it.

## What needs to be done

The brief asks for one command, and grades it on emails we never get to see:

```
python -m rfq parse --emails <dir> --out parsed.json
```

For each email, the command outputs:
- the **classification** (one of 7 kinds),
- the **line items**, each with raw text, a self-contained description, qty, uom and source,
- **`revises` / `duplicate_of`** links,
- a **needs_review** flag with a reason.

It must also meet four hard requirements:

1. **Replayable:** it runs on dev with no API key.
2. **Idempotent:** a second run makes zero model calls.
3. **Fault-tolerant:** one broken email never stops the run.
4. **Cost-reported:** calls, tokens and dollars per email.

**Plus documents:** `RUNNING.md`, `DECISIONS.md` (4 required sections), `AI_USAGE.md`, the `ai-sessions/` logs, a recording of 5 minutes or less, and real git history.

## How it will be achieved: a 6-stage pipeline

| Stage | Who decides | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| **1. MIME** (`rfq/mime.py`) ✅ built | Code | Decodes the email, prefers the HTML version when it holds tables or struck-out text, and splits **current text / quoted reply / forwarded content**. It also flags emails from our own reps and auto-reply headers. |
| **2. Attachments** (`rfq/extract.py`) ✅ built and tested | Code | Identifies files by their bytes, not their names. Handles text PDFs (rebuilt into table rows, struck-out text marked), scanned PDFs (pages turned into images), Excel (**hidden sheets dropped**, merged headings marked, struck cells marked), Word (headings and tables in order, tracked deletions dropped), CSV, and photos. Locked, corrupt or unsupported files return an **error**, never a crash. Page and size limits cover a 300-page PDF. |
| **3. Thread context** | Code | Finds earlier inbox emails in the same thread (via reply headers or subject plus sender), so a reply like "make #3 twelve" can be rebuilt into the full order even when the original isn't quoted. |
| **4. One model call per email** | **Model** | OpenAI with a strict JSON schema and images for scans and photos. The prompt encodes the README rules: classify what the *current* message does, carry headings, sheet names and subject specs into each line without leaking them into other sections, skip struck-out, quoted, price and total lines, and count fuzzy amounts like "a couple" as null. |
| **5. Validation** | Code | Enforces the rules the model must not break: non-request emails get no lines; `source` must be a real filename; uom must come from the allowed list; a request with zero lines or an unreadable attachment is **forced to needs_review** (stops silent losses); and lines taken only from quoted history in a plain RFQ are dropped. **Duplicates** (same customer, same items, later date) and **`revises`** links are decided here in code. |
| **6. Cache, cost, resilience** | Code | Each result is cached under a hash of *the email bytes and the prompt version*, not the rendered images, so the grader's no-key run hits the cache even with different library versions. Failed calls are retried with backoff. A circuit breaker handles the provider being down, and a failure falls back to "rfq + needs_review" rather than losing the email. A report gives calls, tokens and $ per email. |

**Then:**
- **`python -m rfq eval`** scores us against `answer_key.json` on the grader's measures: silent losses, invented lines, lost or phantom requests, accuracy, recall and precision, qty/uom/source, must-mention, and links. That's how we'll know it's right.
- **Docs and git:** RUNNING, DECISIONS, an AI_USAGE outline, commits at each milestone, and parsed.json plus the cache committed.
- **Optional, if time allows:** the catalog matcher.

## What I need from you
The **OpenAI API key** from the assessment email. Without it I can build and test everything except the model calls, and I can't record the cache that has to be committed.

Set it so this session can see it:
```
! setx OPENAI_API_KEY "sk-..."
```
Then restart Claude Code, or tell me another way you'd prefer to supply it. I'll only read it from the environment and never write it to a file.

**Also needs your OK:** the brief requires real git history, so I'd commit at each milestone in the existing repo. `ASSESSMENT.md` currently has uncommitted changes from your editor (escaped `\_` characters) that I'll leave alone.

If you're happy with this, I'll carry on with stages 3–6.

message.content: can it be done using MCP server and MCP client and use that api key to connect my mcp server

content.text:
Yes, it can be done. But it matters where MCP goes, and one part of the question needs correcting first.

**The API key doesn't connect to an MCP server.** The OpenAI key only authenticates calls to OpenAI's model. A local MCP server talks to its client over stdio (a subprocess), which needs no key. The server would read `OPENAI_API_KEY` from its environment and use it for the model calls it makes.

## Option A: MCP inside the graded path (not recommended)
`parse` would start our MCP server as a subprocess. The OpenAI model would then call its tools in a loop (`list_emails`, `read_attachment`, `get_thread`, `submit_lines`…). That's allowed: it's local, and the only outbound call is still OpenAI. But it works against what's graded:
- **Idempotent / replayable:** a tool loop makes a different number of calls each run, so caching it reliably is much harder than one call per email.
- **Cost:** several round-trips per email instead of one, and the cost is harder to predict and report.
- **Fault tolerance:** a subprocess and a protocol layer add new ways to fail on the grader's Windows machine.
- **Control:** in my design, code decides hidden sheets, duplicates, `revises` and review flags. In a tool loop the model decides when to call what, which is the opposite of "what the model decides vs. what your code checks".

## Option B: core pipeline plus an MCP server on top (recommended)
`parse` stays a plain, deterministic, cached pipeline, which is what they run and score. On top of it, an `rfq/mcp_server.py` exposes the same functions as tools:
- `parse_email(path)`: classification and lines, served from the same cache.

"""The model's job, in words and in a strict JSON schema.

The model decides: what the current message does (classification), which lines are requests,
and what context each line inherits.  Everything it returns is re-checked in postprocess.py.
Bump PROMPT_VERSION whenever this file changes meaning: it is part of the cache key.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

PROMPT_VERSION = "p3"

CLASSES = ["rfq", "rfq_revision", "purchase_order", "vendor_quote", "status_inquiry", "auto_reply", "other"]
UOMS = ["EA", "FT", "M", "IN", "BX", "PK", "PR", "DZ", "RL", "LB", "SET", "GAL", "BAG", "CS"]

SYSTEM = """\
You read the RFQ inbox of Ridgeline Industrial Supply (rfq@ridgeline-supply.example), a distributor of \
pipe, fittings, flanges, valves, gaskets, bolting and related industrial supplies. Anyone with an \
address @ridgeline-supply.example is one of OUR reps. Our quotes are numbered Q-26-...; customers' RFQ \
and PO numbers are theirs.

For ONE email you return (1) what the CURRENT message does and (2) exactly the items being asked for, \
each self-contained, as a careful inside-sales rep would type them into a quote.

## Classification - what the current message DOES (not its subject line, not the quoted history)
- rfq: asks us to price / check availability of items.
- rfq_revision: changes a request made earlier in the same thread (quantities, additions, removals).
- purchase_order: commits to buy - a PO document, "please process", "go ahead with items 1-3".
- vendor_quote: a supplier quoting or answering US (e.g. replying to one of our reps' requests for \
pricing). However much it looks like a list of items, it is NOT a customer request.
- status_inquiry: asks about an existing quote or order (update? ETA? tracking?) without asking for new items.
- auto_reply: machine-generated - out-of-office, bounce / delivery failure, read receipt, ticket \
acknowledgement. A bounce of one of OUR outgoing emails is auto_reply even if the attached original lists items.
- other: marketing / promotions / sale flyers, invoices, remittances, job applications, internal chatter, \
"we went with someone else", anything else.
If one of our reps (@ridgeline-supply.example) FORWARDS a customer's email, classify it as the customer's \
email would be classified, and read the rep's own note too. A supplier's newsletter with a price list is \
other, not a request.

## Line items (only for rfq, rfq_revision, purchase_order; otherwise return [])
Which lines count:
- Items in the current message, its attachments and pasted pictures, and - when one of our reps forwards \
a customer's email - the forwarded content.
- NOT items that only appear in quoted earlier messages (they were handled when they arrived). Exceptions: \
an rfq_revision returns the COMPLETE order as now intended (rebuild it from the earlier request it \
modifies - quoted text or the earlier inbox email provided as context - applying every change; dropped \
items are omitted, unchanged items are kept with their original numbering text); a purchase_order that \
accepts items of a quote ("go ahead with 1, 2 and 4") returns exactly the accepted items, taken from \
that quote.
- NOT headings, section titles, column headers, notes, totals / subtotals / "TOTAL QTY" rows, prices, \
freight, taxes, signatures, addresses, reference numbers, crossed-out / struck lines (marked [STRUCK: ...] \
or visibly crossed out in a picture), or old revisions of a document.
- Logos and signature graphics are not item lists.
One line per distinct item requested. Lines written as "same as above", ditto marks (" or ,, under a \
word) inherit the words they repeat.

Fields:
- raw: the line's text as it appears where you found it, close to the source (a table row's cells joined \
with " | " on one line, in the source's column order; for a picture or scan, your faithful reading of it). \
Never put context you added into raw.
- description: the item SELF-CONTAINED: the line's own words plus every heading, section title, merged \
banner, sheet name, column header, form field (e.g. "Material: ASTM A105", "Rating: 150# RF"), subject \
line, "all X are Y" note, or earlier line ("same size", "same as above") that APPLIES to it - and nothing \
that does not apply. Scope matters: a heading applies only to the rows under it, until the next heading; \
a note like "fittings are 150# malleable iron" applies to fittings, never to pipe or valves; "pipe is \
SCH 40" never applies to fittings; a line that states its own value overrides the default ("SCH 80" on a \
line under "ALL SCH 40 UNLESS NOTED" is SCH 80 only); items the customer adds in the email body are not \
covered by a document's header fields unless the customer says so. Include the size. Name the product \
type plainly (pipe, 90 elbow, tee, weld neck flange, gate valve, spiral wound gasket, stud bolt ...). \
NEVER invent a spec, material, rating, schedule or end type the email does not give; if something is \
missing, leave it missing.
- qty: the number as the customer stated it, not converted (12 joints -> 12; 200 ft -> 200). A number \
spelled out is a number ("six" -> 6). Vague amounts ("a couple", "some", "enough for the job") -> null. \
A size, schedule, length, rating, pressure class, part number, line/item number or price is NEVER a quantity.
- uom: one of EA FT M IN BX PK PR DZ RL LB SET GAL BAG CS, as stated by the customer (ft/feet/LF -> FT, \
rolls -> RL, boxes -> BX, pairs -> PR, each/pcs/pieces/joints/jts/lengths/sticks -> EA, sets -> SET). \
null when no unit is stated.
- source: "body" for the email text (including forwarded or quoted text), or the EXACT filename of the \
attachment / pasted image the line came from (use the list of valid sources given).
- location: where you found it (e.g. "sheet 'Rev B' row 5", "page 1 item 12", "body table row 3").

## needs_review - a human must look before anyone quotes it (only for rfq, rfq_revision, purchase_order)
true when the email asks for something you cannot fully read or resolve: the attachment it points at is \
missing (e.g. "BOM attached" but the only attachment is a logo), cannot be opened (password-protected, \
corrupt), is illegible, or the items are only identified by something that is not in the email ("same \
as our last order but double it", "the usual", a revision whose original request is not available). Give \
a short concrete review_reason, and still return every line you COULD read. Otherwise false and null.

## Reasoning fields
Fill message_summary and classification_reasoning first and briefly; they are for an auditor.
"""

LINE_SCHEMA = {
    "type": "object",
    "additionalProperties": False,
    "required": ["raw", "description", "qty", "uom", "source", "location"],
    "properties": {
        "raw": {"type": "string"},
        "description": {"type": "string"},
        "qty": {"type": ["number", "null"]},
        "uom": {"anyOf": [{"type": "string", "enum": UOMS}, {"type": "null"}]},
        "source": {"type": "string"},
        "location": {"type": "string"},
    },
}

SCHEMA = {
    "type": "object",
    "additionalProperties": False,
    "required": [
        "message_summary",
        "classification_reasoning",
        "classification",
        "customer_email",
        "needs_review",
        "review_reason",
        "line_items",
    ],
    "properties": {
        "message_summary": {"type": "string"},
        "classification_reasoning": {"type": "string"},
        "classification": {"type": "string", "enum": CLASSES},
        "customer_email": {
            "type": ["string", "null"],
            "description": "address of the customer actually making the request (the original sender when one of our reps forwards)",
        },
        "needs_review": {"type": "boolean"},
        "review_reason": {"type": ["string", "null"]},
        "line_items": {"type": "array", "items": LINE_SCHEMA},
    },
}

- **No model call at all:** bounces and out-of-office replies (headers and mailer-daemon), bulk marketing (`Precedence: bulk` / `List-Unsubscribe` plus an unsubscribe link), and exact resends (same sender, same attachment bytes, and no new item lines in the body).

The system prompt stays fixed and comes first, so OpenAI's automatic prompt caching bills it at a quarter of the price. The output schema is trimmed, and text-only and vision emails can be routed to different models.
